summary: MPCA Feb-2026 Player Registration sprint (MPCA-147/148/149/151/152/153). Backend 6/6 PASS. Frontend: MPCA-147/148/149/151 PASS; MPCA-153 amend modal is BROKEN due to ReferenceError — 'setAmendOpen is not defined' inside RegistrationsInbox component (state lives on the parent PlayerRegistrations but is not passed down). Return-to-player button correctly removed and Reject button present (verified statically & from live DOM after fix). Also caught an unrelated hydration warning on /register/player/<token> ('<span> cannot be a child of <option>').

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking 'Amend Data' (pr-edit-btn) throws 'ReferenceError: setAmendOpen is not defined'. State (`amendOpen`, `setAmendOpen`) is declared in the parent `PlayerRegistrations` component (line 57) but the child `RegistrationsInbox` (line 242) calls `setAmendOpen(true)` at lines 261 & 266 without receiving it as a prop. Modal never opens; 'Amend Data' & 'Upload Doc on Behalf' buttons are entirely non-functional.
React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Non-blocking but should be fixed for cleanliness.

integration_issues.issue: Because setAmendOpen is undefined, no PATCH is ever issued to /api/player-registrations/<id>/edit from the UI. Backend endpoint works fine (proven by pytest), but UI cannot reach it.

action_items: FIX (critical): In /app/frontend/src/pages/PlayerRegistrations.jsx pass `onOpenAmend` (or `amendOpen`+`setAmendOpen`) as props from PlayerRegistrations (parent) into RegistrationsInbox (child). Simplest fix: hoist the `setAmendOpen` call by lifting the 'amend' action into the parent via a callback prop, OR move the `amendOpen` state into RegistrationsInbox and render RegistrationAmendModal from there.
Fix hydration warning `<span> cannot be a child of <option>` on public player registration form (likely a <select> whose <option>s contain <span> markup).
critical_code_review_comments: PlayerRegistrations.jsx RegistrationsInbox.doAction — dead code path: `setAmendOpen` reference throws at runtime. This means MPCA-153 acceptance criterion 'clicking Amend Data opens the RegistrationAmendModal' is not met.

player_registrations.py — no DELETE endpoint for campaigns; testing agents must use direct mongo cleanup to prevent stale TEST rows. Consider adding an admin-only DELETE /api/player-registration-campaigns/{cid} guarded to MPCA + only when no submissions exist.
player_registrations.py edit_registration silently ignores unchanged fields (good) but returns 200 with no 'edited' event when diff is empty — acceptable but could confuse frontend caller.

success_rate.frontend: 83% (5/6 acceptance points; the amend modal path is fully broken)

seed_data_creation: All test campaigns/registrations created during backend + frontend runs were cleaned up (mongo delete_many on TEST_ email prefix and TEST · title prefix). Verified 0 residuals.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_mpca_feb2026_player_reg_sprint.py — reruns cleanly. The single frontend failure (setAmendOpen ReferenceError) is deterministic; open dev tools on /player-registrations, click Inbox tab, click any Submitted row, click Amend Data → console shows the error. After E1 fixes, re-run the same Playwright test flow and verify [data-testid=pr-amend-modal] appears with ≥5 scalar inputs and ≥5 upload buttons.
rca of the issue: PlayerRegistrations.jsx has the parent component holding `const [amendOpen, setAmendOpen] = useState(false);` at line 57, but the child <RegistrationsInbox> (declared at line 242) calls setAmendOpen(true) at lines 261 (action==='edit') and 266 (action==='upload-doc'). setAmendOpen is not in scope of RegistrationsInbox — it was never passed via props. Fix: (a) hoist the `edit`/`upload-doc` branches out of RegistrationsInbox.doAction, OR (b) pass a callback prop `onOpenAmend={() => setAmendOpen(true)}` from parent into <RegistrationsInbox onOpenAmend=... /> and use that in doAction. Repro: /player-registrations → Inbox tab → click any Submitted row → click 'Amend Data' → runtime overlay shows 'setAmendOpen is not defined'.
